prompt.context: Our client is a large national health care payer (health insurance company, think Aetna) exploring the launch of a new disease management ("DM") program to better serve its 5 million members. The idea is to hire and train a team of "Health Coaches" to specialize in a single disease area (e.g., heart disease, diabetes, etc.). Each Coach will manage a portfolio of patients to reduce the costs of overall health expenditures (e.g., reminders to take drugs, provide limited medical advice, suggested diet, etc.). Studies show that once-a-month contact with each patient reduces health spending by 5%, on average.
prompt.question: Should our client launch the program? If so, what steps should it take?

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape like?
clarifying_info.a: With spiraling health care costs, the industry is under pressure to innovate. Assume client is first to market. Past attempts to purely automate DM have yielded minimal savings.

All activity is conducted remotely via phone/email. Typical profile is a registered nurse who wants to work from home. It is difficult to actually reach patients, so Coaches can contact 8 members per day (assume 25 days per month).

clarifying_info.q: What does a Health Coach cost?
clarifying_info.a: Annual costs per Coach: $60K salary + 20% for other costs (training, benefits, laptop, etc.). There are no other program costs.

exhibits.title: Client's member segmentation by health condition
exhibits.shows: A chart breaking the client's 5 million members into three plan segments (Group, Individual, 65+/Medicare Advantage) and within each segment showing the share of members by health condition (e.g., diabetic, heart disease, healthy, etc.).
exhibits.data: Three segments: Group, Individual, 65+ (Medicare Advantage, premiums funded by government). Each segment shows percentage breakdown of members by disease/health condition. 65+ patients are 20% of total members; diabetics make up ~40% of the 65+ segment.

exhibits.title: Average cost data (Per Member Per Month)
exhibits.shows: A table showing the average Per Member Per Month (PMPM) medical cost for each segment overall and a multiplier representing how much more diabetic members cost relative to the average member in that segment.
exhibits.data: Individual: average PMPM $150, diabetic multiplier 4x; Group: average PMPM $100, diabetic multiplier (not separately stated, derive from context); 65+: average PMPM $300, diabetic multiplier 4x.

framework: Program Savings: segment the 5M members by disease area and per-member cost to identify the highest-value target population; quantify savings from 5% cost reduction
Program Costs: calculate cost per Health Coach (salary + benefits); determine Coach portfolio capacity (patients per Coach); derive cost per patient reached
Break-even / Profitability by segment: compare savings generated per Coach vs. cost per Coach across 65+, Individual, and Group segments
Risks: validate key assumptions (5% savings, reach rate); assess competitive response; consider regulatory and liability issues

questions.prompt: Which member segment and disease area should the client target first, and why?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates should reason that sicker patients drive higher costs, making the 5% savings larger in absolute terms. 65+ (Medicare) patients are the sickest, followed by Individual; Group members are the healthiest (younger, working). Among disease areas, diabetes is the largest chronic condition and—as a behavior-driven disease—most amenable to coaching. Conclusion: focus on 65+ diabetics first.

questions.prompt: How many 65+ diabetic members does the client have?
questions.guidance: Read the 65+ share from Exhibit 1 and apply the diabetic proportion within that segment.

math.setup: 65+ share of total members x diabetic share within 65+ x total members
steps: 20% (65+ share) x 40% (diabetic share within 65+) x 5,000,000 members

questions.prompt: What is the annual cost per Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Add base salary plus the 20% overhead for training, benefits, and equipment.

questions.prompt: How many patients can one Health Coach manage per month (portfolio size)?
questions.guidance: Multiply daily contacts by working days per month.

math.setup: Contacts per day x working days per month
math.answer: 200 patients per month (portfolio size per Coach)

questions.prompt: What are the annual savings generated by one Health Coach managing a portfolio of 65+ diabetics?
questions.guidance: Use the 65+ average PMPM, the diabetic cost multiplier, the 5% savings rate, portfolio size, and 12 months.

math.setup: PMPM for 65+ diabetics x 5% savings x portfolio size x 12 months
steps: 65+ average PMPM = $300; diabetic multiplier = 4x, so 65+ diabetic PMPM = $300 x 4 = $1,200
Annual savings per patient = $1,200 x 5% x 12 = $720
Total savings per Coach = $720 x 200 patients = $144,000

questions.prompt: Is the Health Coach program profitable for the 65+ segment? What about Individual and Group?
questions.guidance: Compare savings per Coach to cost per Coach. 65+ yields $144K savings vs. $72K cost = $72K profit per Coach (2x return). Individual PMPM is $150 (vs. $300 for 65+), so savings are ~$72K per Coach, roughly break-even. Group PMPM is $100, so savings are ~$48K per Coach vs. $72K cost = a loss. Strong candidates note that 65+ is clearly the priority; Individual may be justified on retention/moral grounds; Group is unprofitable as-is.

math.setup: Profit per Coach = Savings per Coach - Cost per Coach; scale to full 65+ diabetic population
steps: Number of Coaches needed for 400,000 patients at 200 per Coach = 2,000 Coaches
Individual check: PMPM $150 x 4 x 5% x 12 x 200 = $72K savings - $72K cost = $0 (break-even)
Group check: PMPM $100 x 4 x 5% x 12 x 200 = $48K savings - $72K cost = -$24K (loss)
math.answer: 65+ segment: $72K profit per Coach, $144M total profit per year. Individual: break-even. Group: loss of ~$24K per Coach.

brainstorming.prompt: There are 650K Group diabetics left uncoached. Is there a way to make the Group segment profitable?

categories.name: Increase coaching efficiency
ideas: Bi-monthly or quarterly contact instead of monthly to reduce Coach workload
Automated correspondence (apps, emails, SMS) supplementing human contact
Group coaching sessions (one Coach contacts multiple members simultaneously)

categories.name: Additional revenue sources
ideas: Charge employers a per-member fee for coaching their insured workers
Seek government grants or public-health subsidies
Bundle with wellness programs that employers already pay for

categories.name: Targeting within the segment
ideas: Since 5% is the average, identify high-risk Group diabetics likely to respond with savings well above 5%
Use predictive analytics to prioritize members with highest expected cost reduction
Focus only on the highest-cost Group diabetics to raise average PMPM above break-even threshold

recommendation: The client should launch the Health Coach disease management program, initially focused on Type 2 diabetes in the 65+ Medicare Advantage segment
At full deployment (2,000 Coaches managing 400,000 patients), the program generates $144M in annual profit—a 2x return on Coach cost

After validating assumptions in a pilot, the client should expand to the Individual segment (break-even, but valuable for retention and social mission) and explore ways to make the Group segment viable
risks: The 5% average cost reduction may not hold in practice; a pilot is needed to validate the assumption
Coach portfolio capacity (200 patients/month) assumes consistent patient reachability, which may be optimistic
Expanding enrollment of high-cost diabetic members could increase total health expenditures even after the 5% savings
Regulatory and liability issues if Coaches provide incorrect medical advice
Competitive response: if program is successful, competitors will replicate it quickly
next_steps: Launch a controlled pilot to validate the 5% savings assumption and Coach capacity
Scale to the full 65+ diabetic population once the pilot confirms economics
Evaluate the Individual segment launch in parallel (break-even but strategically valuable)
Conduct analysis on the Group segment to identify if targeting high-responders or employer-funded models make it profitable
Assess opportunity to sell Health Coach services to other payers (pricing and regulatory hurdles to consider)
